summary: Compose the Johnson-Hinnov hydrogen Lyman-alpha photon rate and line emissivity of an explicit one-dimensional profile from the bound r-coefficient and Saha-population assets, with the saved composition's frozen constants and operation order preserved bit for bit.

identity.relation: the saved Lyman-alpha relation: photon_rate = A[0] * (r_ion0 + r_ion1 * n0 / saha1) * saha_level2 and emissivity = (13.6057 * (0.25 - 1/9) eV) * photon_rate * 1.602177e-19, with the r coefficients and Saha populations bound from the already-integrated SciRel assets
identity.direction: paired electron density and temperature, ground-state neutral density, explicit JH payload -> Lyman-alpha emissivity and photon rate per sample
identity.definition: The bound r asset evaluates r02 (ion 0) and r12 (ion 1) for principal level 2 with the saved 1e32 sentinel density overwrite; the bound Saha asset evaluates the level-1 and level-2 populations from the caller's density and temperature; the contraction applies the saved Einstein coefficient A[0] and the frozen emissivity factors in the saved operation order.
identity.model: the saved formal implementation's explicit-payload radiation composition (KN1DPy/jh_related/lyman_alpha.py:42-64), re-expressed as an ordered composition of the bound SciRel assets; no hidden state
identity.coordinates: electron density in m^-3, electron temperature in eV, ground-state neutral density in m^-3; emissivity in W m^-3, photon rate in m^-3 s^-1
identity.boundary: the composed domain is the intersection of the bound assets' contracts: density and temperature in (0, 1e32), n0 in (0, 1e32), non-empty one-dimensional paired arrays; only the source-complete no_null=1 branch is admitted; outputs must be finite and strictly positive
assumptions: The bound r asset's saved 1e32 sentinel density overwrite carries into the composition: the r channels do not depend on the caller's density values beyond shape and validation.
The bound Saha asset enforces its documented < 1e32 domain, so the composed domain is narrower than the saved radiation callable's; on the shared domain the outputs are bit-identical.
The coefficient and Einstein tables are caller-supplied data; this graph composes them, it does not certify any table.
No external atomic-physics reference is bound: the saved package records that residual as validation_oracle_gap.

inputs.name: density_m3
inputs.description: Electron densities; consumed by the Saha populations and validated by the bound r asset.
inputs.constraints: A non-empty one-dimensional array, finite and strictly positive and below 1e32 (the bound Saha asset's domain limit), paired with the temperatures.

inputs.name: temperature_ev
inputs.description: Electron temperatures; clipped to the temperature-knot range by the bound assets.
inputs.constraints: A one-dimensional array of the same shape, finite and strictly positive and below 1e32.

inputs.name: n0_m3
inputs.description: Ground-state neutral densities entering the excited-population correction term.
inputs.constraints: A one-dimensional array of the same shape, finite and strictly positive and below the 1e32 source null sentinel.

inputs.name: jh_payload
inputs.description: The read-only Johnson-Hinnov coefficient payload mapping with the exact fields DKnot, TKnot, order, LogR_BSCoef, LogS_BSCoef, LogAlpha_BSCoef, A_Lyman, A_Balmer.
inputs.dtype: mapping of arrays and an integer
inputs.constraints: Validated by this graph against the saved exact eight-field contract (the complete field set including fields the branch does not numerically consume, one-dimensional non-decreasing finite knots, order field 4 consumed by FITPACK as the spline degree describing exactly 77 coefficients, every field finite) before any evaluation; never mutated.

inputs.name: no_null
inputs.description: The source branch selector passed through to the bound assets.
inputs.constraints: Only the source-complete no_null=1 branch is admitted; any other value fails closed.

outputs.name: emissivity_w_m3
outputs.description: The Lyman-alpha line emissivity with the saved energy factor.
outputs.constraints: Finite for every accepted input; the saved composition gates finiteness only, so a caller-supplied Einstein coefficient of zero returns zero rates (no emission) and a negative one returns negative values (source parity).

outputs.name: photon_rate_m3_s
outputs.constraints: Finite for every accepted input; the saved composition gates finiteness only, so a caller-supplied Einstein coefficient of zero returns zero rates (no emission) and a negative one returns negative values (source parity).

preconditions: The caller supplies a complete, consistent JH payload; the graph composes it, it does not construct or certify one.
The profile inputs stay inside the composed domain (all values finite, positive and below 1e32).
supported: Lyman-alpha photon rates and emissivities for explicit hydrogen profiles on any consistent caller-supplied payload.
Rejecting malformed profiles, n0 outside the saved contract, incomplete payloads and non-1 no_null before any evaluation.
excluded: Emissivities whose energy factor differs from the saved frozen factor; the saved arithmetic is preserved, not repaired.
Two-dimensional or spatially gridded profiles: the bound assets accept one-dimensional profiles only.
Coefficient or Einstein tables validated against an external atomic-physics reference; none is bound.

failure_semantics.invalid_input: Raises ValueError with a message naming the condition when the profiles are not non-empty same-shaped 1-D finite positive arrays, when density or temperature reach 1e32 (the composed Saha domain), when n0 is not finite, positive and below the 1e32 sentinel, when no_null is not 1, when the payload violates the saved exact eight-field contract (field set, knots, order, 77-coefficient geometry, finiteness), or when required inputs are missing; bound-asset validation failures propagate unchanged.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: Raises ValueError when the composition produces a non-finite photon rate or emissivity; per source parity the gate is finiteness-only, so a zero or negative caller-supplied Einstein coefficient returns zero or negative values rather than being rejected.
failure_semantics.nonconvergence: Not applicable; this TaskGraph is an ordered DAG with no feedback loop.
failure_semantics.partial_results: Never returned; a rejected call produces no diagnostic.

example.description: Evaluate the Lyman-alpha emission on a synthetic validated payload and confirm the saved energy factor and the composed-domain rejections.
example.code:
import numpy as np
from scipy.interpolate import RectBivariateSpline
from scirel.diagnostics import solve_hydrogen_jh_lyman_alpha_emission

temperature_axis = np.linspace(-1.0, 1.0, 11)
density_axis = np.linspace(30.0, 32.0, 7)
spline = RectBivariateSpline(temperature_axis, density_axis, np.add.outer(temperature_axis, density_axis), kx=4, ky=4)
temperature_knots, density_knots = spline.get_knots()
coefficients = spline.get_coeffs()
payload = {
    "DKnot": density_knots,
    "TKnot": temperature_knots,
    "order": 4,
    "LogR_BSCoef": np.zeros((coefficients.size, 2, 5)),
    "LogS_BSCoef": coefficients.copy(),
    "LogAlpha_BSCoef": coefficients.copy() + 0.25,
    "A_Lyman": np.linspace(3.0e8, 1.0e5, 15),
    "A_Balmer": np.linspace(4.4e7, 2.0e4, 15),
}
density = np.array([1.0e20, 5.0e20])
temperature = np.array([5.0, 30.0])
n0 = np.array([1.0e17, 2.0e18])
result = solve_hydrogen_jh_lyman_alpha_emission(density_m3=density, temperature_ev=temperature, n0_m3=n0, jh_payload=payload)
assert result["photon_rate_m3_s"].shape == density.shape
assert np.all(np.isfinite(result["emissivity_w_m3"])) and np.all(result["emissivity_w_m3"] > 0.0)
saved_factor = 13.6057 * (0.25 - 1.0 / 9.0)
np.testing.assert_array_equal(result["emissivity_w_m3"], saved_factor * result["photon_rate_m3_s"] * 1.602177e-19)
try:
    solve_hydrogen_jh_lyman_alpha_emission(density_m3=density, temperature_ev=temperature, n0_m3=np.full(2, 1.0e32), jh_payload=payload)
except ValueError as error:
    assert "n0_m3" in str(error)
else:
    raise AssertionError("an n0 at the 1e32 sentinel must be rejected")
try:
    solve_hydrogen_jh_lyman_alpha_emission(density_m3=density, temperature_ev=temperature, n0_m3=n0, jh_payload=payload, no_null=0)
except ValueError as error:
    assert "no_null=1" in str(error)
else:
    raise AssertionError("no_null=0 must be rejected")
example.expected: Finite strictly positive emissivity and photon rate with the inputs' shape; the emissivity equals the saved frozen factor times the photon rate times the elementary charge; an n0 at the 1e32 sentinel and no_null=0 are rejected.

The environment-gated replay establishes exact bit-level agreement with the saved KN1DPy composition on the packaged coefficient payload and the compared rejections only. No test establishes the coefficient table or the Einstein coefficients against an external atomic-physics reference: the saved package records that residual as validation_oracle_gap. KN1DPy's strict D1 qualification is withdrawn; the saved bundle supports bounded historical development comparison only. Expert recognition, version-level trust and distribution licensing remain pending.
known_limitations: The saved implementation multiplies BOTH the Lyman-alpha and the Balmer-alpha photon rate by 13.6057 * (0.25 - 1/9) eV, the n=3 -> 2 photon energy; the returned Lyman emissivity therefore carries that factor rather than the physical n=1 -> 2 energy 13.6057 * (1 - 1/4) eV. The photon rate is unaffected. Whether a successor should repair the Lyman factor is an open expert-review question; this asset preserves the executed arithmetic.

The output gate is finiteness-only, exactly as saved: a caller-supplied Einstein coefficient of zero returns zero photon rate and emissivity (no emission) and a negative one returns negative values; sign and scale of the line are the caller's data responsibility.

The composed domain narrows the saved composition: density and temperature must stay below 1e32 because the bound r56 Saha asset enforces its documented limit, while the saved radiation callable admits any positive finite values (only n0 is bounded on the saved arm). The narrowing is declared and witnessed by the replay tests.
The asset evaluates caller-supplied coefficient and Einstein tables; it does not certify any table's physics (validation_oracle_gap).

The saved bundle sits in the re-review archive and KN1DPy's strict D1 qualification is withdrawn; the historical replay evidence cannot be upgraded to qualified-L1 provenance without a new strict freeze and independent review of the source project.
